question.worked_solution:
To evaluate this expression, we use PEMDAS.

First, consider the expression inside the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-8)^{2}\times \frac{3}{64}\end{aligned}
$$

Applying PEMDAS to this expression, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-8)^{2}\times \frac{3}{64} & = \\ 64\times \frac{3}{64} & = \\ \frac{64}{1}\times \frac{3}{64} & = \\ \frac{64\times 3}{1\times 64} & = \\ \frac{\cancel{64}\times 3}{1\times \cancel{64}} & = \\ 3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-3)\times ((-8)^{2}\times \frac{3}{64}) & = \\ (-3)\times 3 & = \\ -9\end{aligned}
$$
